chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Henry Red Allen: diminished-against-major lines and small-band records
summary: Red Allen played riffs that fit, right or wrong; Horace made small-band records with him, J.C. Higginbotham and Don Stovall.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Uh-huh. True. Well, we've mentioned Henry Red Allen in this several times, and I do have his name on the list.

Yeah, Red Red was a great trumpet player. No greater ever lived, man. And he was another one of those trumpet players that didn't know, musically, but and what not, but all he had to do was -- play it for him, you know. He Hit it rather, and he would play a riff to fit with it, whether it was wrong or not. You know? And then finished against major. He The featured that, and of course, he was well known for that.

And I made quite a few records with Red with a small band, you know. Red did a little singing too, you know, on some of these sides, and we had J. C. Higgenbotham in there. There was a saxophonist, alto saxophonist named Don Stovall. Does that name ever ring a bell with you?
